title: NASA Psyche spacecraft begins continuous propulsion phase
excerpt: The spacecraft is accelerating toward the asteroid Psyche using its solar electric propulsion system.
bodyHtml:
NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory announced on October 22, 2026, that the Psyche spacecraft has entered a phase of near-continuous propulsion. Following a Mars gravity assist, the mission began using its electric propulsion system almost constantly on September 28.

The spacecraft uses a Hall effect system, which expels charged atoms of the inert gas xenon to create thrust. According to the mission's navigation lead, Don Han, the thrusters will operate approximately 90% of the time until the spacecraft reaches the asteroid Psyche in the summer of 2029. During this cruise, the spacecraft will reach speeds exceeding 100,000 mph relative to an observer on Earth.

Mission engineers are managing torque generated by the swirling ions within the thrusters using reaction wheels. The spacecraft launched with nearly 2,400 pounds of xenon in seven fuel tanks and has used about one third of that supply. This remaining propellant will assist the spacecraft as it orbits the asteroid Psyche during a two-year prime science mission.
